Vegan Food in Italy

By Richard Prouse · Not yet checked on the ground · Updated 2026-11-17

Draft. This guide has not yet been checked on the ground. It is hidden from search engines until it is.

Italy's peasant cooking (cucina povera) is full of dishes that are vegan by tradition: pizza marinara, pasta with tomato, bean soups and Sicilian chickpea fritters. Watch for Parmesan grated on top, anchovies in sauces, and fresh egg pasta.

How easyEasy
Word for veganvegano / vegana
Try firstPizza marinara

Traditional dishes in Italy that are vegan or can be

  • Pizza marinara

    Pizza marinara

    Vegan by tradition

    Tomato, garlic, oregano and olive oil. No cheese by tradition.

  • Pasta and beans

    Pasta e fagioli

    Usually vegan: check

    Check for pancetta or Parmesan rind.

  • Chickpea fritters

    Panelle

    Vegan by tradition

    Palermo street food made from chickpea flour.

  • Chickpea flatbread

    Farinata

    Vegan by tradition

    Ligurian chickpea flatbread baked in olive oil.

  • Caponata

    Caponata

    Usually vegan: check

    Sweet-and-sour Sicilian aubergine stew.

  • Pasta with tomato

    Pasta al pomodoro

    Ask for it vegan

    Vegan with dried pasta; ask for no Parmesan.

What to watch for in Italy

  • Parmesan (parmigiano) grated on pasta and soups
  • Anchovies (acciughe) in sauces
  • Fresh egg pasta (pasta all'uovo)
  • Butter (burro) in northern dishes and risotto

How to ask for vegan food in Italian

Show this to your server, or print it:

Sono vegano (vegana). Non mangio carne, pesce, uova, latticini né miele. Senza parmigiano, per favore.

Why Italy

Italy is the number 4 most-visited country in the world, with 60.6 million international arrivals in 2024 (UN Tourism).
